name: TesterArmy

team.summary: Oskar, Szymon, and Piotr are building TesterArmy, backed by Y Combinator (P26).

evidence.quote: Hey HN - we’re Oskar, Szymon, and Piotr, and we’re building TesterArmy

product.summary: TesterArmy is an agentic end-to-end testing platform that runs checks before deployment and in production using natural language specifications and AI agents.

evidence.quote: TesterArmy is an agentic testing platform that runs end-to-end checks before deployment and in production.
we let you specify your tests in natural language and handle everything in between.

size_hint.summary: Targeting software engineering and development teams looking to speed up testing and avoid manual QA bottlenecks.

evidence.quote: TesterArmy's agents test every pull request like real users while your engineers ship.

competitors.summary: Commenters and site copy mention competitors like Cypress, Revyl, mobileboost.io, Rainforest QA, Playwright, Momentic, Spur, QA Wolf, Mabl, and BrowserStack.

evidence.quote: We use cypress heavily for our core flows which has a similar ai prompt thing
evidence.author: msencenb

evidence.quote: I'm curious how your mobile testing compares to https://revyl.com
evidence.author: tcoff91

evidence.quote: Rainforest QA, for example, has been in this space for a while and also happens to be a YC company.
evidence.author: fny

why_now.summary: Advances in coding agents and large language models enable natural language test definition and autonomous browser navigation.

evidence.quote: AI coding tools have made it dramatically faster to write and ship code, but testing is still a bottleneck.

risks.risk: Third-party SaaS reliance and security/privacy concerns regarding outsourcing testing and credentials.

evidence.quote: also I feel uneasy about outsourcing this part with all the security issues these days.
evidence.author: zuzululu

evidence.quote: config overhead and potential security leaks makes it a no go
evidence.author: negamax

risks.risk: Token cost economics and stability of running continuous LLM-driven agents for every test execution.

evidence.quote: How would this compare to the token costs of running an agent the whole time for each test?
evidence.author: poisonborz

founder_depth.why: Founders are technical and participating in YC, but limited explicit background or prior exits are detailed in the sources.

evidence.quote: Hey HN - we’re Oskar, Szymon, and Piotr, and we’re building TesterArmy

shipping_evidence.why: Product is live with a functional demo, CLI integration, and documented feature releases.

evidence.quote: Over the past few months, we scaled from 0 to 30+ teams using our product every day.

demand_signal.why: Strong HN engagement (132 points, 69 comments), 30+ teams using the product, and positive customer testimonials.

evidence.quote: Over the past few months, we scaled from 0 to 30+ teams using our product every day.

defensibility.why: Provides workflow depth and integrations, but some commenters note similarity to existing tools and wrapper-like concerns.

evidence.quote: This is a solved problem, there are many that do this. Can't believe YC would fund this in 2026.
evidence.author: mogili

analysis.thesis_fit_reason: TesterArmy is an AI-native developer and engineering tool used by software teams to automate end-to-end testing via agents, paid for through tiered usage plans.
analysis.case_summary: Strong initial adoption and active user feedback contrast with skepticism regarding token costs and defensibility against existing testing frameworks and tools.
would_change_my_mind: Published unit economics demonstrating profitability despite underlying LLM and vision model token costs.
Data showing low test flake rates compared to traditional deterministic code frameworks.
Enterprise customer case studies showing long-term retention and replacement of legacy test suites.
data_gaps: Exact revenue figures or pricing tier adoption metrics.
Detailed public GitHub repository with open source components.
Quantitative reliability benchmarks across standard test suites.
